newsitem.title: UK: British Aerospace pretax profits jump.
newsitem.headline: British Aerospace pretax profits jump.

text.p: British Aerospace announced a sharp jump in annual profits on Wednesday, topping most analysts' forecasts, and it said a booming order book and focus on cost cutting promised more to come.

Pretax profits leapt by over 80 percent to 425 million pounds last year from 234 million in 1995, with underlying profits before exceptional charges rising 38 percent to 456 million pounds from 330 milion last time.
"1996 was a successful year for British Aerospace... and reflects the drive for continuous improvement in productivity and cost elimination," chairman Bob Bauman said in the results statement.

The company said a 1.9 billion pound British government order for Nimrod maritime patrol aircraft helped boost its order book to an all-time high of 19.4 billion pounds by the end of the year, compared to 17.1 billion a year ago. Group turnover rose 12.2 percent last year to 7.44 billion pounds.

Chief executive Sir Richard Evans said: "Our order book provides clear visibility for trading over the next few years, enabling senior management to spend time progressing the strategic relationships that will shape the nature and context of our industry as it moves into the next century."
